title: Symmetry-Aware Scene-Based Non-Uniformity Correction for Real-Time Infrared Image Enhancement
content: Infrared focal-plane arrays are affected by pixel-to-pixel response variation, stripe artifacts, and random noise, which can impair image interpretation and target tracking in rapidly changing scenes. This study presents a symmetry-aware, scene-based non-uniformity correction method for real-time infrared image enhancement. The method forms a local reference with a cross-shaped four-neighborhood operator that weights the horizontal and vertical directions equally and is invariant to 90° rotations. This directional symmetry provides a balanced estimate of the local response, while per-pixel gain and offset coefficients are updated by gradient descent to reduce the difference between the corrected response and the local reference. The method was implemented on a 640 × 512 field-programmable gate array prototype. Hardware tests over 1000 frames yielded a processing latency below 1 ms per frame. On 12 datasets at a high noise level, the proposed method achieved a mean peak signal-to-noise ratio of 26.15 dB and a mean structural similarity index of 0.73, exceeding the strongest baseline by 0.78 dB and 0.05, respectively. Experiments on real non-uniform infrared sequences further showed effective suppression of stripe and random noise while preserving edges and background brightness. These results indicate that local directional symmetry is a useful design prior for efficient infrared non-uniformity correction and supports deployment on vehicle-, ship-, and airborne imaging platforms.
